paper.title: Multi-Armed Bandits with Metric Movement Costs

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-armed Bandits with Movement Costs (finite metric space)
unmapped: switching cost given by a fixed, known metric Delta(i,j) in [0,1] on the action set (movement cost), rather than unit switching cost
regret rates governed by covering/packing complexity of the metric
settings.definition_quote: There is a set $K$, possibly infinite, of actions ... equipped with a fixed and known metric $\dist$ that determines a cost $\dist(i,j) \in [0,1]$ for moving between any pair of actions ... an adversary fixes a sequence $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T : K \mapsto [0,1]$ ... (in particular, we assume an oblivious adversary). ... the total cost at round $t$ is given by $\ell_t(i_t)+\dist(i_{t-1},i_t)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-armed Bandits with Movement Costs (infinite metric space, Lipschitz losses)
unmapped: movement cost given by the same known metric with respect to which losses are Lipschitz
rate governed by the upper Minkowski dimension of the metric space
settings.definition_quote: One natural assumption, which is common in previous work, is to assume that the loss functions $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T$ are all $1$-Lipschitz with respect to the metric $\dist$.

algorithms.name: Slowly Moving Bandit (SMB) on general HST
SMB applied to constructed dominating HST (tree approximation of the metric, with depth adjustment)
Discretization + SMB for infinite metric spaces

symbols.C_c: covering complexity of the metric, sup_{0<eps<1} eps * N^c_eps(Delta)

source.label: thm:upper
source.quote: Let $(K,\dist)$ be a finite metric space over $\abs{K} = k$ elements with diameter $\le 1$ and \upper $\dimu = \dimu(\dist)$. There exists an algorithm such that for any sequence of loss functions $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T$ guarantees that $\mregret(\ell_{1:T},\dist) = \tO\Lr{ \max\Lrset{ \dimu^{1/3} T^{2/3}, \sqrt{kT} } }$.

results.notes: Movement regret = E[sum losses + sum movement costs] - min_i sum losses; losses deterministic (oblivious), so expected regret against best fixed action. Tree construction depends on T, hence known horizon. Algorithm described as efficient.

symbols.C_p: packing complexity of the metric, sup_{0<eps<1} eps * N^p_eps(Delta)

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Let $(K,\dist)$ be a finite metric space over $\abs{K} = k$ elements with diameter $\ge 1$ and \low $\diml = \diml(\dist)$. For any algorithm there exists a sequence $\ell_1,\ldots, \ell_{T}$ of loss functions such that $\mregret(\ell_{1:T},\dist) = \wt{\Omega}\Lr{ \max\Lrset{ \diml^{1/3} T^{2/3}, \sqrt{kT} } }$.

results.notes: Proof sketch embeds Dekel et al. unit-switching lower bound in a packing; sqrt(kT) from Auer et al. Matches upper bound up to logs since C_p <= C_c <= 2 C_p.

symbols.d_M: upper Minkowski dimension of the metric space (d_M >= 1)

source.label: thm:coverdim
source.quote: Let $(K,\dist)$ be a metric space with diameter $\le 1$ and upper Minkowski dimension $d = \cdim(\dist)$, such that $d\ge 1$. There exists a strategy such that for any sequence of loss functions $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T$, which are all $1$-Lipschitz with respect to $\dist$, guarantees that $\mregret(\ell_{1:T},\dist) = \tO\Lr{ T^\frac{d+1}{d+2} }$.

results.notes: Hidden constant may depend on the metric (covering constant C). Discretization requires computing a covering; compute not explicitly stated for infinite spaces.

symbols.C_tree: complexity (covering = packing) of the HST metric

conditions: metric is an HST metric Delta_T induced by a tree with all leaves at the same depth

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Assume that the metric $\dist = \distT$ is a metric specified by a tree $\cT$ which is a HST with $\depth(\cT) = H$ and \upperlow $\dim(\cT)=\dim$. Then, for any sequence of loss functions $\ell_1,\ldots, \ell_T$, \cref{alg:smb} guarantees that $\mregret(\ell_{1:t},\distT) = \O\LR{ \frac{H\log{\dim}}{\eta} + \eta \dim H 2^H T + H 2^{-H} T }$.

symbols.C_tree: complexity (covering = packing) of the HST metric

conditions: metric is an HST metric Delta_T induced by a 2-HST with all leaves at the same depth

source.label: lem:smb-tree
source.quote: Let $(K,\distT)$ be a metric space defined by a $2$-HST $\cT$ with $\depth(\cT) = H$ and \upperlow $\dim(\cT)=\dim$. Using SMB algorithm we can achieve the following regret bound: $\mregret(\ell_{1:T},\distT) = \O\LR{ H \sqrt{2^H T \dim \smash{\log\dim }} + H 2^{-H} T }$.

results.notes: Same as the tuned bound stated in Theorem 16 (second display).

conditions: metric is an HST tree metric Delta_T

source.label: lem:tree
source.quote: For any tree $\cT$ and time horizon $T$, there exists a tree $\cT'$ (over the same set $K$ of $k$ leaves) that satisfies the conditions of \cref{cor:smb-goodtree}, such that $\dist_{\cT'} \ge \dist_{\cT}$ and $\dim(\cT') = \dim(\cT)$. Furthermore, $\cT'$ can be constructed efficiently ... Hence, applying SMB to the metric space $(K,\dist_{\cT'})$ leads to $\mregret(\ell_{1:T},\distT) = \tO\Lr{ \max\Lrset{\dim(\cT)^{1/3} T^{2/3}, \sqrt{kT}} }$.

results.notes: Tree-metric special case of Theorem 7. Corollary 12 gives the same bound for 'well-behaved' trees satisfying depth conditions; not recorded separately.
